title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 8. Beholding Sri Govardhana and Other Places
html:
Krishnadasa tells of Vraja's move to Nandishvara and shows the Lord Govardhana: the Mano-Ganga, where Krishna took the gopis out in a boat, and the place where He levied a toll on them — here the Lord, contemplating that pastime, loses outward awareness and weeps over a stone; the circle of the rasa dance, the place of the Annakuta, the Deities Hariraya and Gopalaraya, the ponds at the foot of the hill; praising Govardhana, the Lord breaks into dance

Verse 1

पुनश्च कंसभीतेन संमन्त्र्य स्वजनैः सह।
नन्दीश्वरे निवासश्च चक्रे नन्देन सव्रजम्॥१॥

punaśca kaṁsabhītena saṁmantrya svajanaiḥ saha|
nandīśvare nivāsaśca cakre nandena savrajam||1||

punah — again; cha — and; kamsa-bhitena — fearing Kamsa; sammantrya — taking counsel; sva-janaih — with his people; saha — together; nandishvare — at Nandishvara; nivasah — a dwelling; cha — and; chakre — was made; nandena — by Nanda; sa-vrajam — with all Vraja.

1"Then Nanda, fearing Kamsa, again took counsel with his people and settled with all Vraja at Nandishvara1.

Verse 2

गोवर्धनगिरौ रम्ये मनःस्वर्गनदीतटे।
नित्यं विहरतः कृष्णरामौ सखिसमन्वितौ॥२॥

govardhanagirau ramye manaḥsvarganadītaṭe|
nityaṁ viharataḥ kṛṣṇarāmau sakhisamanvitau||2||

govardhana-girau — on Govardhana Hill; ramye — lovely; manah-svarga-nadi-tate — on the bank of the heavenly river of the mind (the Mano-Ganga); nityam — always; viharatah — sport; krishna-ramau — Krishna and Rama; sakhi-samanvitau — with their friends.

2On lovely Govardhana Hill, on the bank of the heavenly river Manasa2, Krishna and Rama sported continually with Their friends.

Verse 3

इन्द्रगर्वनिरासार्थं सप्तवर्षो हरिः किल।
गिरिं दधार हर्षेण स्वानां रक्षां विचिन्तयन्॥३॥

indragarvanirāsārthaṁ saptavarṣo hariḥ kila|
giriṁ dadhāra harṣeṇa svānāṁ rakṣāṁ vicintayan||3||

indra-garva-nirasa-artham — to dispel Indra's pride; sapta-varshah — seven years old; harih — Hari; kila — it is said; girim — the hill; dadhara — held up; harshena — joyfully; svanam — of His own people; raksham — the protection; vichintayan — thinking of.

3To dispel Indra's pride, Hari, they say, at seven years of age joyfully held up the hill, thinking of the protection of His own people3.

Verse 4

नौक्रीडां कृतवान् कृष्णो गङ्गायां रसकौतुकी।
कुर्वन्ति मथुरां गोष्ठे लोका गमननिर्गमे॥४॥

naukrīḍāṁ kṛtavān kṛṣṇo gaṅgāyāṁ rasakautukī|
kurvanti mathurāṁ goṣṭhe lokā gamananirgame||4||

nau-kridam — boating sport; kritavan — made; krishnah — Krishna; gangayam — on the Ganga (the Mano-Ganga); rasa-kautuki — eager for the play of rasa; kurvanti — make; mathuram — (the way) to Mathura; goshthe — in the cowherd settlement; lokah — the people; gamana-nirgame — in going and coming.

4Eager for the play of rasa, Krishna went boating on the Ganga — there where the people of the cowherd settlement go to Mathura and back4.

Verse 5

अत्र दाननिमित्तं हि प्रस्तरांशं विशन् हरिः।
गोपिका रमयन् रेमे भक्तानुग्रहकाम्यया॥५॥

atra dānanimittaṁ hi prastarāṁśaṁ viśan hariḥ|
gopikā ramayan reme bhaktānugrahakāmyayā||5||

atra — here; dana-nimittam — for the sake of the toll; hi — indeed; prastara-amsham — into a cleft of the rocks; vishan — entering; harih — Hari; gopikah — the gopis; ramayan — delighting; reme — sported; bhakta-anugraha-kamyaya — wishing to show grace to His devotees.

5Here Hari, wishing to show grace to His devotees, entered a cleft in the rocks to levy a toll, and sported, delighting the gopis."

Verse 6

पश्यन् श्रीगौरचन्द्रः स रसनकुतुकाद्बाह्यवृत्तिं विहाय
वंशीश्रीवत्सवेत्रैः कुसुमकिसलयैर्मण्डितं श्यामधाम।
दानं मे देहि राधे रसवति विमले दानपात्रेऽवदद्यो
ह्येवं तं स्तौति गौरः स जयति खलु भो राधिकाप्राणनाथः॥६॥

paśyan śrīgauracandraḥ sa rasanakutukādbāhyavṛttiṁ vihāya
vaṁśīśrīvatsavetraiḥ kusumakisalayairmaṇḍitaṁ śyāmadhāma|
dānaṁ me dehi rādhe rasavati vimale dānapātre'vadadyo
hyevaṁ taṁ stauti gauraḥ sa jayati khalu bho rādhikāprāṇanāthaḥ||6||

pashyan — beholding; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; sah — He; rasana-kutukat — out of eagerness to taste rasa; bahya-vrittim — outward awareness; vihaya — abandoning; vamshi-shrivatsa-vetraih — with flute, Shrivatsa and stick; kusuma-kisalayaih — with flowers and fresh leaves; manditam — adorned; shyama-dhama — the dark Splendour; danam — the toll; me — to Me; dehi — give; radhe — O Radha; rasavati — O you full of rasa; vimale — O pure one; dana-patre — to a worthy recipient; avadat — said; yah — who; hi — indeed; evam — thus; tam — Him; stauti — praises; gaurah — Gaura; sah — He; jayati — glory to; khalu — indeed; bhoh — oh (interjection); radhika-prana-nathah — the Lord of Radhika's life.

6Beholding this, Sri Gaurachandra, in His eagerness to taste rasa, abandoned outward awareness: He saw the dark Splendour adorned with flute, Shrivatsa mark5 and stick, with flowers and fresh leaves — Him who said, "Give Me the toll, Radha, you who are full of rasa, you pure one — to Me, a worthy recipient!" And thus Gaura praises Him: "Glory, oh, glory to Him, the Lord of Radhika's life!"

Verse 7

तदैव सहसा भक्तिरसाविष्टोऽखिलेश्वरः।
पाषाणं सजलं कृत्वा लिलेप शिरसि रुदन्॥७॥

tadaiva sahasā bhaktirasāviṣṭo'khileśvaraḥ|
pāṣāṇaṁ sajalaṁ kṛtvā lilepa śirasi rudan||7||

tada — then; eva — at once; sahasa — suddenly; bhakti-rasa-avishtah — possessed by the rasa of devotion; akhila-ishvarah — the Lord of all; pashanam — the stone; sa-jalam — wet; kritva — making; lilepa — anointed; shirasi — His head; rudan — weeping.

7And at once the Lord of all, suddenly possessed by the rasa of devotion, weeping, wetted the stone with His tears and anointed His head with it.

Verse 8

गिरेः पूर्वे कुण्डयुग्मं पश्य कृष्णरसप्रदम्।
अस्य दक्षिणपार्श्वे च रासमण्डलमुत्तमम्॥८॥

gireḥ pūrve kuṇḍayugmaṁ paśya kṛṣṇarasapradam|
asya dakṣiṇapārśve ca rāsamaṇḍalamuttamam||8||

gireh — of the hill; purve — to the east; kunda-yugmam — the pair of ponds; pashya — behold; krishna-rasa-pradam — that bestow the rasa of Krishna; asya — of it; dakshina-parshve — on the south side; cha — and; rasa-mandalam — the circle of the rasa dance; uttamam — excellent.

8"Behold: to the east of the hill are two ponds6 that bestow the rasa of Krishna, and to the south of them the excellent circle of the rasa dance.

Verse 9

श्रीराधाकृष्णयो रासविलासस्थानमत्र वै।
पश्य प्रेमरसैः पूर्णैर्भक्तैरेव विभाव्यते॥९॥

śrīrādhākṛṣṇayo rāsavilāsasthānamatra vai|
paśya premarasaiḥ pūrṇairbhaktaireva vibhāvyate||9||

shri-radha-krishnayoh — of Sri Radha and Krishna; rasa-vilasa-sthanam — the place of the rasa pastime; atra — here; vai — indeed; pashya — behold; prema-rasaih — with the rasas of love; purnaih — filled; bhaktaih — by devotees; eva — only; vibhavyate — is perceived.

9Here is the place where Sri Radha and Krishna enjoyed the rasa pastime; behold — only devotees filled with the rasas of love can perceive it."

Verse 10

राधामाधवयोरैक्यात्तत्तद्भावविभावितः।
तत्तल्लीलानुकरणं गौराङ्गः समदर्शयत्॥१०॥

rādhāmādhavayoraikyāttattadbhāvavibhāvitaḥ|
tattallīlānukaraṇaṁ gaurāṅgaḥ samadarśayat||10||

radha-madhavayoh — with Radha and Madhava; aikyat — because of His oneness; tat-tat-bhava-vibhavitah — stirred by each of Their moods; tat-tat-lila-anukaranam — the re-enactment of each of Their pastimes; gaurangah — Gauranga; samadarshayat — displayed.

10Being one with Radha and Madhava and stirred by each of Their moods, Gauranga re-enacted each of Their pastimes.

Verse 11

भावप्रकाशकं कृष्णं प्राह ब्राह्मणसत्तमः।
पर्वतोपरि संपश्य राधिकाराधनस्थलम्॥११॥

bhāvaprakāśakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ prāha brāhmaṇasattamaḥ|
parvatopari saṁpaśya rādhikārādhanasthalam||11||

bhava-prakashakam — who was revealing these moods; krishnam — to Krishna; praha — said; brahmana-sattamah — the best of brahmanas; parvata-upari — on the hill; sampashya — behold; radhika-aradhana-sthalam — the place of Radhika's worship.

11To Krishna, who was revealing these moods, the best of brahmanas said, "Behold on the hill the place of Radhika's worship.

Verse 12

अन्नकूटस्थलं चात्र सुरेशगर्वनाशकम्।
इन्द्रोत्पातं हरिर्वीक्ष्य गोवर्धनधरोऽभवत्॥१२॥

annakūṭasthalaṁ cātra sureśagarvanāśakam|
indrotpātaṁ harirvīkṣya govardhanadharo'bhavat||12||

anna-kuta-sthalam — the place of the Annakuta; cha — and; atra — here; sura-isha-garva-nashakam — which destroyed the pride of the lord of the gods; indra-utpatam — Indra's onslaught; harih — Hari; vikshya — seeing; govardhana-dharah — the Holder of Govardhana; abhavat — became.

12And here is the place of the Annakuta7, which crushed the pride of the lord of the gods: seeing Indra's onslaught, Hari became the Holder of Govardhana.

Verse 13

पर्वतोपरि तं पश्य हरिरायाख्यकं विभुम्।
तस्योपरि दक्षिणेऽपि गोपालरायसंज्ञकम्॥१३॥

parvatopari taṁ paśya harirāyākhyakaṁ vibhum|
tasyopari dakṣiṇe'pi gopālarāyasaṁjñakam||13||

parvata-upari — on the hill; tam — that; pashya — behold; hariraya-akhyakam — called Hariraya; vibhum — Lord; tasya — of Him; upari — above; dakshine — to the south; api — also; gopalaraya-samjnakam — named Gopalaraya.

13Behold on the hill the Lord called Hariraya, and above Him, to the south, the one named Gopalaraya8.

Verse 14

इन्द्रगर्वनिरासे च ब्रह्मणा चोदिता सती।
सुरभी स्वर्णदीतोयेनाभिषेकं मुदाकरोत्॥१४॥

indragarvanirāse ca brahmaṇā coditā satī|
surabhī svarṇadītoyenābhiṣekaṁ mudākarot||14||

indra-garva-nirase — when Indra's pride had been dispelled; cha — and; brahmana — by Brahma; chodita — urged; sati — the good; surabhi — Surabhi; svarnadi-toyena — with the water of the heavenly river; abhishekam — the ceremonial bathing; muda — joyfully; akarot — performed.

14When Indra's pride had been dispelled, the good Surabhi9, urged by Brahma, joyfully bathed with the water of the heavenly river

Verse 15

गोविन्दस्य च वेदाद्यैः सेवितस्य महोत्तमे।
कृतागस्को महेन्द्रोऽपि यं स्तुत्वा निर्भयोऽभवत्॥१५॥

govindasya ca vedādyaiḥ sevitasya mahottame|
kṛtāgasko mahendro'pi yaṁ stutvā nirbhayo'bhavat||15||

govindasya — of Govinda; cha — and; veda-adyaih — by the Vedas and others; sevitasya — served; maha-uttame — at the supreme festival; krita-agaskah — who had committed an offence; maha-indrah — great Indra; api — even; yam — whom; stutva — praising; nirbhayah — fearless; abhavat — became.

15Govinda, who was served by the Vedas and the rest at that supreme festival; and even great Indra, who had offended, became free from fear by praising Him.

Verse 16

सर्वपापहरं कुण्डं पश्य पर्वतदक्षिणे।
अस्योपरि पञ्चकुण्डं ब्रह्मरुद्रेन्द्रसूर्यकम्॥१६॥

sarvapāpaharaṁ kuṇḍaṁ paśya parvatadakṣiṇe|
asyopari pañcakuṇḍaṁ brahmarudrendrasūryakam||16||

sarva-papa-haram — that removes all sins; kundam — the pond; pashya — behold; parvata-dakshine — south of the hill; asya — of it; upari — beyond; pancha-kundam — the five ponds; brahma-rudra-indra-suryakam — of Brahma, Rudra, Indra and Surya.

16Behold to the south of the hill the pond that removes all sins; and beyond it are five ponds — of Brahma, Rudra, Indra and Surya,

Verse 17

मोक्षेतिकुण्डसंज्ञं च सर्वपापहरं शुभम्।
पश्यन् गौरहरिः कृष्णः प्रेम्णोवाच द्विजं प्रभुः॥१७॥

mokṣetikuṇḍasaṁjñaṁ ca sarvapāpaharaṁ śubham|
paśyan gaurahariḥ kṛṣṇaḥ premṇovāca dvijaṁ prabhuḥ||17||

moksha-iti-kunda-samjnam — the pond named "Moksha"; cha — and; sarva-papa-haram — removing all sins; shubham — auspicious; pashyan — beholding; gaurahari — Gaurahari; krishnah — Krishna; premna — with love; uvacha — said; dvijam — to the brahmana; prabhuh — the Lord.

17and the auspicious pond named 'Moksha', which removes all sins." Beholding them, the Lord Gaurahari — Krishna — said lovingly to the brahmana:

Verse 18

धन्योऽयं गिरिराज एव जगति श्रीकृष्णरामौ मुदा
यत्र क्रीडत एव सन्ततमहो गोपालबालैः सह।
एवं जल्पति प्रेमपूर्णरसदः श्रीगौरचन्द्रः स्वयं
श्रीगोवर्धन एव साग्रहमपि तं पूजयन् नृत्यति॥१८॥

dhanyo'yaṁ girirāja eva jagati śrīkṛṣṇarāmau mudā
yatra krīḍata eva santatamaho gopālabālaiḥ saha|
evaṁ jalpati premapūrṇarasadaḥ śrīgauracandraḥ svayaṁ
śrīgovardhana eva sāgrahamapi taṁ pūjayan nṛtyati||18||

dhanyah — blessed; ayam — this; giri-rajah — king of mountains; eva — alone; jagati — in the world; shri-krishna-ramau — Sri Krishna and Rama; muda — joyfully; yatra — where; kridatah — play; eva — indeed; santatam — ever; aho — ah!; gopala-balaih — with the cowherd boys; saha — together; evam — thus; jalpati — speaks; prema-purna-rasa-dah — the giver of the rasa of perfect love; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; svayam — Himself; shri-govardhanah — Sri Govardhana; eva — himself; sa-agraham — eagerly; api — too; tam — Him; pujayan — worshipping; nrityati — dances.

18"Blessed in the world is this king of mountains alone, where Sri Krishna and Rama — ah! — ever play joyfully with the cowherd boys!" So speaks Sri Gaurachandra Himself, the giver of the rasa of perfect love — and Sri Govardhana himself, eagerly worshipping Him, begins to dance.

Thus ends the eighth sarga, "Beholding Sri Govardhana and Other Places" (Shri-govardhana-adi-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Nandishvara: the hill at Nandagrama where, according to tradition, Nanda settled.
  2. That is, the Mano-Ganga (Manasi-Ganga), the sacred lake at Govardhana.
  3. Bhagavata Purana 10.25.
  4. The sense of the second half of the verse is obscure in the text; the rendering is conjectural.
  5. Shrivatsa: the mark on Vishnu's chest.
  6. Apparently Radha-kunda and Shyama-kunda.
  7. Annakuta ("mountain of food"): the offering to Govardhana which the cowherds, on Krishna's advice, made in place of the sacrifice to Indra (Bhagavata Purana 10.24).
  8. Hariraya and Gopalaraya: Deities of Krishna on Govardhana.
  9. Surabhi: the celestial cow, mother of all cows; the bathing of Krishna (Govinda) after the lifting of Govardhana is told in Bhagavata Purana 10.27.
